segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: A hurricane at the Gulf, Ukraine talks in Miami, and Ebola spreads
bullets: Hurricane Isaias: 110 mph, Gulf oil shut in
Russian strikes; U.S. envoys meet Ukraine in Miami
Ebola: 8,750 cases; Kenya, Netherlands
Mortgage rates highest since 2023

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Friday, October ninth.
Today: Hurricane Isaias builds off the Mississippi, more than half of Gulf oil is shut in, and U.S. envoys sit down with Ukraine in Miami.
Plus Ebola numbers, a mortgage rate that keeps climbing, and a new legal fight over who gets into the White House. Let's go.

segments.strap: HURRICANE ISAIAS: 110 MPH, 200 MILES FROM THE MISSISSIPPI
segments.headline: Hurricane Isaias

graphic.title: Hurricane Isaias, Gulf Coast
bullets: About 200 miles SSE of the Mississippi River mouth
Storm-surge and hurricane warnings in effect
El Niño shear vs. warm water (AP)

lines.text: Hurricane Isaias leads the show. The National Hurricane Center's Advisory Eleven puts its winds at one hundred ten miles an hour. The center is about two hundred miles south-southeast of the mouth of the Mississippi River.
Storm-surge and hurricane warnings are still in effect. That is the official word.
A.P. describes two forces pulling against each other. Wind shear from El Niño could hold the storm down. Warm Gulf water could feed it.
So the storm is deciding what kind of day it wants to have. Everyone on the coast would like to vote.
One note from the desk. Claude's morning search could not find an official advisory, and older local reports disagreed about the storm's strength. The hurricane center's advisory is the source here.

segments.strap: 62.89% OF GULF OIL OUTPUT SHUT IN FOR ISAIAS
segments.headline: Gulf oil shut-ins

graphic.title: Gulf production shut in
bullets: Marine Minerals Administration estimate
Based on operator reports through 11 a.m. CDT, Oct 8
Brent topped $104 Thursday (AP)

lines.text: The Marine Minerals Administration estimates sixty-two point eight nine percent of Gulf oil production is shut in because of Isaias. For natural gas, it is fifty-seven point three five percent. Those figures come from operator reports through eleven a.m. Central on Thursday.
More than half of the Gulf's oil, switched off by weather.
A.P. reports Brent crude topped one hundred four dollars on Thursday. That is a press report, and the link between the two is not stated in the capture.

segments.strap: RUSSIAN STRIKES HIT UKRAINE; U.S. ENVOYS MEET IN MIAMI
segments.headline: Ukraine: strikes and talks

graphic.title: Ukraine: strikes and a Miami meeting
bullets: Reuters: at least 20 killed Oct 7, incl. children
A.P.: 2 killed in Zaporizhzhia, Ivano-Frankivsk
Witkoff and Kushner meet Ukraine in Miami
Winter energy-strike campaign under way

lines.text: Ukraine. Reuters, via Global Banking and Finance, reports Russia hit Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones on October seventh. At least twenty people were killed, including children. Industrial and energy sites were damaged.
President Zelenskiy called it one of the most brutal attacks of the war. It came on Putin's birthday. A missile destroyed an apartment block in Pryluky, in the Chernihiv region.
Newer strikes: A.P. reports two people killed in the Zaporizhzhia and Ivano-Frankivsk regions, and five wounded in Zaporizhzhia. Another strike wounded three in the Kyiv region.
And today in Miami, Axios says U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are to meet Ukrainian negotiators and European officials. They bring proposals to break the stalemate.

The think tank Critical Threats, a solo analyst source, says Russia began its winter energy-infrastructure strike campaign in late September. It cites the U.N. counting more than fifteen thousand two hundred eighty civilian casualties in the first eight months of this year, fifty-five percent more than in twenty twenty-five. All of this is reported by press and analysts, not confirmed here.

segments.strap: TRUMP: NO U.S. ATTACK ON IRAN BEFORE NOV. 3 MIDTERMS
segments.headline: Iran and the midterms

graphic.title: Trump on Iran
bullets: A.P.: Trump says no attack before the midterms
He wrote that talks with Tehran were productive
That is his claim, via A.P.

lines.text: A.P. reports President Trump said the United States would not attack Iran before the November third midterm elections. He wrote that discussions with Tehran were productive.
That is a claim from the president, reported by A.P. No agreement or text was produced in the capture.
A promise with an expiration date of election day. The robot may want to circle that.

segments.strap: EBOLA: 8,750 CONFIRMED CASES, 4,208 DEATHS
segments.headline: Ebola outbreak

graphic.title: Ebola outbreak
bullets: C.D.C. Oct 8: one confirmed case in Kenya
W.H.O.: spread to Alimbongo, North Kivu
Netherlands evacuated an infected health worker
Kenya: first case died in Nairobi; 28 contacts

lines.text: Ebola. The C.D.C.'s October eighth update counts eight thousand seven hundred fifty confirmed cases and four thousand two hundred eight confirmed deaths across the affected countries. It reports one confirmed case in Kenya and none in the United States.

The World Health Organization says the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to the Alimbongo health zone in North Kivu. It also notes the Netherlands evacuated an infected health worker for medical care.
On Kenya, CTV News reports the first case was a traveler from Congo, on October sixth. The patient died in Nairobi. Twenty-eight contacts have been identified, and Africa C.D.C. sent a team.
The same report says the outbreak is slowing in Ituri and spreading in North and South Kivu. It found no second Kenyan case.

segments.strap: MORTGAGE RATE 7.40%, HIGHEST SINCE NOV. 2023
segments.headline: Money: rates and markets

graphic.title: Rates and markets
bullets: Freddie Mac: 7th straight weekly rise
Bitcoin low $80,544, back to $82,551
Next CPI Oct 14, 8:30 ET (carried)

lines.text: Freddie Mac says the thirty-year fixed mortgage rate rose to seven point four percent. That is its seventh weekly increase and the highest since November twenty twenty-three.
Seven weeks in a row. Somewhere a house is looking at its price tag and sweating.

Stocks, per A.P.: the S and P five hundred fell half a percent to seven thousand seven hundred sixty-five. The Dow rose a tenth of a percent to fifty-one thousand two hundred thirty-one. The Nasdaq fell one point three percent.
MarketScreener says Bitcoin rose nine tenths of a percent to eighty-two thousand five hundred fifty-one dollars, after dipping to eighty thousand five hundred forty-four.
One date ahead. A morning search carried forward that the next consumer price report is October fourteenth at eight-thirty Eastern. That is carried from earlier days, not freshly sourced.

segments.strap: OPENAI DEFENDS FIRING THREE SAFETY RESEARCHERS
segments.headline: OpenAI safety firings

graphic.title: OpenAI and the safety researchers
bullets: OpenAI says they mishandled sensitive information
Researchers: firings chilled safety talk
Reported by A.P. and The Verge

lines.text: A.I. news. A.P. reports OpenAI defended firing three safety researchers for allegedly mishandling sensitive information. The researchers said the dismissals chilled internal safety discussion.
The Verge says OpenAI is doubling down on the decision. Two accounts, one dispute, and no outside finding yet on who is right.

segments.strap: ANTHROPIC LAUNCHES FREE OPEN-SOURCE SECURITY SCANS
segments.headline: Anthropic OSS Scanner

graphic.title: Anthropic OSS Scanner
bullets: Opt-in; free periodic scans
Run by Anthropic's strongest models
Reports are model-generated, no human review

lines.text: Anthropic launched an opt-in tool called the O.S.S. Scanner. Open-source projects get free periodic security scans from its strongest models.
The company says the reports are model-generated and not reviewed by a human. So a robot checks your code and no person looks at the answer. Read it with that in mind.

segments.strap: U.S. SUSPENDS MICROSOFT, ADOBE, INFOSYS, TATA FROM GREEN-CARD PROGRAM
segments.headline: Labor certification suspensions

graphic.title: Permanent Labor Certification suspended
bullets: Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Capgemini
HCL, Infosys, Tata, Wipro
Microsoft: 80% of ~6,000 H-1B filings were existing staff

lines.text: TechCrunch reports the administration suspended eight companies from the Permanent Labor Certification Program, a step in the green-card process for skilled foreign workers. They are Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Capgemini, H.C.L., Infosys, Tata and Wipro.
Microsoft said eighty percent of its roughly six thousand H-1B applications last fiscal year were for existing employees. That is the company's statement, as reported.

lines.text: In court, A.P. reports lawyers for three news organizations asked a federal judge to block the White House from barring their reporters while their case goes forward.
Reporters arguing in court about being let into the room. Which is a bit like asking the room to describe itself.

A.P. says it is the first government body to sue over the project.

Hunger strike in URL; headline only

Only the headline reached our desk, so we have no more detail than that. We will say so rather than guess.

segments.strap: JAPAN CLOUD RANSOMWARE OUTAGE HITS 495 CUSTOMERS
segments.headline: Cyber: Japan cloud and ASOS

graphic.title: Cyber incidents
bullets: IDC Frontier blames ransomware
East Japan Region 1 cloud; govt clients
ASOS: customer names, contacts may be exposed

lines.text: Cyber. BleepingComputer reports IDC Frontier attributed an East Japan Region One cloud outage to ransomware. It affected four hundred ninety-five business and municipal customers.
And TechCrunch reports the British retailer ASOS confirmed unauthorized notifications went to customers through a third-party platform. Names and contact details may have been accessed.

segments.strap: NASA CREW-12 SPLASHES DOWN AFTER 237 DAYS IN SPACE
segments.headline: Crew-12 splashdown

graphic.title: Crew-12 splashdown
bullets: Pacific splashdown off Los Angeles, 11:34 a.m. EDT
Crew-13 launched Oct 1 (Spaceflight Now)
SpaceX plans mobile-carrier business (The Verge)

lines.text: Space. N.A.S.A.'s SpaceX Crew Twelve Dragon splashed down in the Pacific off Los Angeles at eleven thirty-four a.m. Eastern. Four astronauts came home after two hundred thirty-seven days on the space station.
Two hundred thirty-seven days. Their first meal back had better be enormous.
Their replacements are already up. Spaceflight Now says Crew Thirteen launched October first. Separately, The Verge headline says SpaceX plans to become a major mobile carrier.

segments.strap: WAYMO CLOSES $5 BILLION LOAN; TSMC AND SAMSUNG NUMBERS
segments.headline: Business: Waymo, TSMC, Samsung

graphic.title: Waymo, TSMC, Samsung
bullets: Waymo: first debt financing, term loan
TSMC Sept revenue +54.6% year on year
Samsung Q3 guide: revenue KRW 195 trillion

lines.text: Business, from the companies themselves. Waymo closed its first debt financing, a five billion dollar term loan, to support commercial expansion.

T.S.M.C. reported September revenue of five hundred eleven point eight six billion Taiwan dollars. That is up fifty-four point six percent from a year ago and down six tenths of a percent from August.
Samsung's third-quarter guidance estimates operating profit of one hundred seven point four trillion won, on revenue of one hundred ninety-five trillion won.

segments.strap: FEMA AGAIN DENIES ILLINOIS DISASTER RELIEF
segments.headline: FEMA denies Illinois

graphic.title: FEMA and Illinois
bullets: Chicago-area August tornadoes, damaging winds
Illinois request denied a second time
Indiana's request for the same storm was granted

lines.text: FEMA again denied Illinois' request for disaster relief after August tornadoes and damaging winds in the Chicago region, NPR Illinois reports. Indiana's request for the same storm was granted.

lines.text: Also today, all from The Verge, mostly headlines only. Microsoft three sixty-five Family subscribers can share A.I. benefits. Microsoft is overhauling Windows Search for Windows Eleven.
Apple will reportedly debut its first touchscreen MacBook in about three weeks. That is a rumor. And A.M.D. says it will bring FSR Four to handhelds by the end of the year.
California is trying to stop robot-versus-human cage matches. And The Verge headline says the U.S. plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.
We only have the headline on that last one, so we will leave it there.

segments.strap: TAMPA BAY BEATS DALLAS 24-16; GUARDIANS FORCE GAME 5

graphic.title: Division Series and Thursday NFL
bullets: Tampa Bay 24, Dallas 16

lines.text: Sports. Tampa Bay beat Dallas twenty-four to sixteen on Thursday night. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels started in place of the injured Baker Mayfield.
In baseball, Cleveland beat Chicago nine to five in Game Four of the Division Series. That forces a deciding Game Five on Saturday, October tenth, at eight p.m. Eastern.
